column2: Taking a water-pot, a rosary, a staff, the life-restoring herb, the perfected knowledge and the scriptures, the lord of practitioners,
placing once in the heart the three-pointed form encircled by waves of blazing sparks of fire, burns up all sin born over crores of births.
Placed on poison, it destroys poison; placed on the body, it destroys leprosy; one who has committed the killing of an embryo and the like is purified in his own body by this divine means.
For those seized by great planetary spirits, one should contemplate it blazing within the heart; then the fierce spirits quickly perish.
Tied on the necks of children it is a constant protection; it surely destroys boils, lumps and spider-poison.
When disease arises, one should offer fuel-sticks with ghee and milk; doing so at the three junctions for a month destroys all diseases.
I see nothing impossible in the three worlds, moving and unmoving; whatever perfection he desires, that he surely obtains.
Some, having worshipped the lord of beasts a hundred and eight times, take seven kinds of earth from an anthill, a cremation ground and a crossroads,
mix them with red sandal and knead them with cow's milk, and make an image of the lion six finger-breadths in size;
one should anoint it and write on birch-bark with gorochana; and the knower of mantras, tying it to Narasimha's neck,
should recite without count after worshipping it in a reservoir; he should recite for a week with senses controlled.
Within a moment the whole earth becomes covered with water. Or one should worship Narasimha on the top of a dry tree,
and reciting the essence a hundred and eight times, one can stop rain. Tying it in a cage, the best practitioner should whirl it;
a great wind will come within a moment, without doubt; and he should quickly hold it again with water seven times seven.
If the practitioner buries that image at someone's door, that person's family will be destroyed; when it is dug up, it brings peace.
Therefore, O tigers among sages, one should always worship with devotion that very mighty king of beasts, who grants the fruit of every desire.
Freed from all sins, he goes to Vishnu's world. Brahmins, kshatriyas, vaishyas, women, shudras and the lowest castes,
having worshipped with devotion that best of gods who bears the form of a lion, are freed from evils and sorrows arising over crores of births.
Having worshipped that best of gods they obtain what they desire — godhood, lordship over the immortals and the state of a Gandharva, O brahmins,
the state of a Yaksha or Vidyadhara, and whatever else they wish. Having seen, praised, bowed to and worshipped the Man-Lion,
men obtain kingship, heaven and rare liberation. A man who sees Narasimha obtains the fruit he desires;
freed from all sins, he goes to Vishnu's world. Having seen once with devotion that god in lion form,
one is freed from evils and sorrows arising over crores of births. In battle, in distress, in a fortress, when oppressed by thieves, tigers and the like,
in a wilderness, when life is in doubt, amid poison, fire and water, from kings and oceans, and when afflicted by planets, diseases and the like,
a man who remembers him is freed from all such troubles. As great darkness perishes when the sun rises,
so at the sight of him calamities perish. Magic pills, collyrium, sandals for the netherworld and elixirs,
and other things desired, one obtains when Narasimha is pleased. Whatever desires a man meditates on while worshipping the Man-Lion,
those desires he obtains; there is no doubt. Having seen that lord of the gods, worshipped him with devotion and bowed,
one obtains tenfold the fruit of ten horse sacrifices; freed from all sins and adorned with all virtues,
rich in every desire, free from old age and death, in a golden celestial car hung with networks of bells,
rich in every desire, moving at will, radiant, coloured like the young sun, hung with pearl necklaces,
accompanied by a hundred divine women and resounding with divine Gandharvas, raising twenty-one generations, joyful and happy like a god,
praised by Apsarases, the man goes to Vishnu's world. Having enjoyed excellent pleasures there in Vishnu's world, O best of brahmins,
accompanied by Gandharvas and Apsarases, taking a four-armed form, happiness that delights the mind until the dissolution of beings,

when his merit is exhausted he comes here and in an excellent family of yogins becomes a brahmin versed in the four Vedas, master of the Vedas and their limbs; taking up the yoga of Vishnu, he then attains liberation.
On that auspicious, delightful shore, near Krishna, Shveta then had a temple built with auspicious features,
a hundred and one bow-lengths to the south of the god of gods. Then, O best of brahmins, by Shveta, of white stone,
that Lord Shveta Madhava, like the moon, was made; and he himself performed the consecration duly as prescribed.
Having given gifts to the twice-born, the poor, the helpless and ascetics, the king then, in the presence of Madhava,
suddenly fell to the ground, and reciting Om and the twelve-syllable mantra, keeping silence, for one month in samadhi,
fasting, the illustrious one remained fixed in Vishnu's state. At the end of the recitation he began to praise the lord of gods:

Om, salutation to Vasudeva, salutation to Sankarshana, to Pradyumna and Aniruddha, and salutation to Narayana.
brahmapuran:59:35	Salutation to the many-formed, to the universal form, to the creator, the one without qualities, beyond reasoning, the pure, whose deeds are bright.
brahmapuran:59:36	Om, salutation to the lotus-naveled, the source of the one born from the lotus; salutation to the lotus-coloured one, salutation to you with a lotus in hand.
brahmapuran:59:37	Om, salutation to the lotus-eyed, the thousand-eyed, the bountiful; salutation to the thousand-footed, whose arms and wrath are a thousand.
brahmapuran:59:38	Om, salutation to the Boar, the giver of boons, the wise, the most excellent, the adorable, the refuge, Achyuta.
brahmapuran:59:39	Om, salutation to the one in child's form, radiant like a young lotus, whose eyes are the morning sun and moon, with hair like munja grass, the wise one.
brahmapuran:59:40	Salutation ever to Keshava, and salutation to Narayana; to Madhava, the most excellent; to Govinda, salutation again and again.
brahmapuran:59:41	Om, salutation ever to Vishnu, the god whose seed is wealth; salutation to Madhusudana, the pure one who bears the rays.
brahmapuran:59:42	Salutation to Ananta, the subtle; salutation to the bearer of the Shrivatsa; salutation to Trivikrama, and to the one wearing divine yellow garments.
brahmapuran:59:43	Salutation to you, creator; salutation again and again to the protector and sustainer; salutation to the one who is the qualities, and again and again to the one beyond qualities.
brahmapuran:59:44	Salutation to the one in dwarf form, to the one of the dwarf's deeds, to the one with the dwarf's eyes, to the one borne by the dwarf.
brahmapuran:59:45	Salutation to the delightful, the adorable; salutation to the one of unmanifest form, beyond reasoning, the pure, and the remover of fear.
brahmapuran:59:46	To the ship across the ocean of worldly existence, the tranquil one who is his own form, to Shiva of gentle form, to Rudra, and to the one who carries across;
brahmapuran:59:47	to the one who breaks existence and grants the enjoyments of existence, to the one whose form is the aggregate of existence, the maker of the creation of existence, salutation.
brahmapuran:59:48	Om, salutation to the one of divine form, whose breath is Soma and fire, whose hair is the rays of moon and sun, beneficial to cows and brahmins.
brahmapuran:59:49	Om, salutation to the one whose form is the Rik, whose form is the pada and krama recitations; salutation to you praised by the Rik, salutation to the means of the Rik.
brahmapuran:59:50	Om, salutation to the sustainer of the Yajus, bearing the form of the Yajus, to be worshipped by the Yajus, delighted in, the lord of the Yajus.
brahmapuran:59:51	Om, salutation, O lord of Shri, O god, bearer of Shri, the excellent, beloved of Shri, the self-controlled, to be meditated on by yogins, the yogin.
brahmapuran:59:52	Om, salutation to the one whose form is the Saman, excellent in the sound of the Saman; Om, salutation to the gentle one of the Saman, the knower of the yoga of the Saman.
brahmapuran:59:53	To the Saman, the one sung in the Saman; Om, salutation to the bearer of the Saman, the knower of Saman sacrifices, salutation to the maker of the Saman.
brahmapuran:59:54	Salutation to the one whose head is the Atharvan, whose form is the Atharvan; salutation to the one whose feet are the Atharvan, salutation to the maker of the Atharvan.
brahmapuran:59:55	Om, salutation to the one with a diamond head, slayer of Madhu and Kaitabha, dwelling in the waters of the great ocean, the recoverer of the Vedas.
brahmapuran:59:56	Salutation to the one of blazing form, salutation to Hrishikesha; salutation to you, the Lord, salutation to you, Vasudeva.
brahmapuran:59:57	Narayana, salutation to you, salutation to the benefactor of the world; Om, salutation to the destroyer of delusion and the breaker of existence,
brahmapuran:59:58	salutation to the giver of the goal, salutation to the remover of bonds; salutation to the maker of the splendours of the three worlds, whose form is splendour,
brahmapuran:59:59	to the lord of yogins, the pure, to Rama, to the one who carries across, to happiness, to the one with happy eyes, salutation to the bearer of good deeds,
brahmapuran:59:60	to Vasudeva, the adorable, salutation to Vamadeva, to the maker of the bodies of the embodied and the breaker of divisions,
brahmapuran:59:61	whose body is adored by the gods, salutation to you with divine crown; salutation to the dwelling of dwellings, who conducts the affairs of dwelling.
brahmapuran:59:62	Om, salutation to the maker of wealth and giver of wealth and dwelling; salutation to the one whose form is sacrifice, the lord of sacrifice, the yogin,
brahmapuran:59:63	the lord who makes the yoga of ascetics, salutation to the bearer of the limbs of sacrifice; salutation to Sankarshana, and to the crusher of Pralamba,
brahmapuran:59:64	bearing the plough, whose speed surpasses the roar of clouds; salutation to the knowledge of the knowers, O you devoted to Narayana.
brahmapuran:59:65	I have no kinsman but you to carry me across hell, O Lord; therefore I bow to you with all my being, O you who love the humble.
brahmapuran:59:66	Whatever impurity there is, of body or of mind, O Keshava, there is no other who can wash it away but you, O Achyuta, lord of the gods.
brahmapuran:59:67	Abandoning all associations I have come to you; may my association be with you for the attainment of the Self, O Keshava.
brahmapuran:59:68	I know worldly existence, O Keshava, to be a painful calamity very hard to cross; afflicted by the threefold suffering, I have therefore come to you for refuge.
brahmapuran:59:69	The whole world is deluded by your maya through its desires and drawn away by greed and the rest; therefore I have taken refuge in you.
brahmapuran:59:70	There is no happiness at all, O Vishnu, for an embodied being in worldly existence; but as the mind turns toward you, O lord of sacrifice,
brahmapuran:59:71	so one gains absolute happiness free from fruits. I am lost, devoid of discrimination; the world appears afflicted.
brahmapuran:59:72	O Govinda, save me from worldly existence; you must lift me out. For one sunk in the waters of delusion in the uncrossable ocean of existence, there is no rescuer but you, O lotus-eyed one.
Thus praised by King Shveta, O brahmins, in that divine, excellent region famed as Purushottama,
considering his devotion, the god of gods, teacher of the world, Hari, came before the king surrounded by all the gods,
like a dark cloud, with eyes long as lotus petals, the wise one holding Sudarshana, a blazing disc, at the tip of his hand;
in his left hand shone the very radiant Panchajanya, like the waters of the milk ocean, spotless and like the moon.

The glorious Lord, whose banner is the king of birds, bearing mace, Sharnga and sword, said: "Well done, O king, whose mind is excellent. Choose what you desire; blessings on you; I am pleased with you, O sinless one."
Hearing that supreme nectar-like speech of the god of gods, Shveta, his mind absorbed in him, bowed his head and said:

If I am your devotee, O Lord, grant me the highest boon: the imperishable state of Vishnu beyond the abode of Brahma,
brahmapuran:59:80	spotless, free of passion, pure, devoid of attachment to worldly existence — I wish to go to that state by your grace, O lord of the world,
brahmapuran:59:81	that delightful, supreme, faultless state which all the gods, sages and perfected yogins do not reach.

You will go to the supreme abode after enjoying the nectar of kingship; passing beyond all worlds, you will go to my world.
brahmapuran:59:83	Your fame here, O king of kings, will go to the three worlds, and my presence will always be here.
brahmapuran:59:84	All the gods and Danavas will sing of the 'Shveta Ganga'; and even touching the water of the Shveta Ganga with the tip of a kusha blade, O king of kings,
brahmapuran:59:85	my devotees who are composed will go to heaven. Whoever goes to this image named Madhava, radiant as the moon,
brahmapuran:59:86	like conch and cow's milk, destroyer of all sins, and bows once with devotion to her with eyes like white lotuses,
brahmapuran:59:87	leaving all worlds, is honoured in my world; there, for Manu-periods, surrounded by divine maidens,
brahmapuran:59:88	sweetly sung to and attended by Siddhas and Gandharvas, he enjoys abundant pleasures as he wishes with my own people.
brahmapuran:59:89	Falling from there and coming here, he becomes a human brahmin, knower of the Vedas and their limbs, glorious, rich in enjoyments and long-lived,
brahmapuran:59:90	rich in elephants, horses, chariots and vehicles, surrounded by wealth and grain, pure, handsome, very fortunate and blessed with sons and grandsons.
brahmapuran:59:91	Reaching Purushottama again, at the root of the banyan or in the ocean, giving up his body while remembering Hari, he then goes to the state of peace.
Pure in body, speech and mind, absorbed in him and thinking of nothing else, free from all pairs of opposites, free from passion and envy,
having bathed at the delightful wish-fulfilling banyan, one should circumambulate Janardana three times with great composure.
By seeing it one is freed from sin arising over seven births and obtains abundant merit and the desired goal, O brahmins.
I shall tell its names and its measure in each age, O brahmins, in order, beginning with the Krita age.
Vata, Vateshvara, Krishna and Puranapurusha, O brahmins — these are declared the names of the banyan in the Krita and following ages.
A yojana, three-quarters of a yojana, half a yojana and half of that — this is declared the measure of the wish-fulfilling tree beginning with the Krita age.
Having bowed to that banyan with the prescribed mantra, one should go facing south three hundred bow-lengths,
to where Vishnu is seen at the charming gate of heaven — the log drawn up from the waters of the ocean, endowed with every virtue.
Having bowed to it and then worshipped it fully, one is freed from all diseases and the like, and from sins, planets and so on.
Having first seen Ugrasena, going to the ocean by the gate of heaven, sipping water and being pure there, meditating on the supreme Narayana,
one should then place the eight-syllable mantra on the hands and body — "Om namo narayanaya," which the wise recite.
What need of many mantras that bewilder the mind? The mantra "Om namo narayanaya" accomplishes every aim.
The waters are called 'nara' because they are the offspring of Nara; since they were formerly Vishnu's abode (ayana), he is remembered as Narayana.
The Vedas are devoted to Narayana, the twice-born are devoted to Narayana, sacrifices are devoted to Narayana, rites are devoted to Narayana;
the earth is devoted to Narayana, water is devoted to Narayana, fire is devoted to Narayana, the sky is devoted to Narayana;
the wind is devoted to Narayana, the mind is devoted to Narayana; egoity and intellect both have Narayana as their self.
Past, present and future, whatever is called a living being, gross, subtle and supreme — all has Narayana as its self.
All objects beginning with sound, the senses beginning with the ear, Prakriti and Purusha — all have Narayana as their self.
In water, on land, in the netherworld, in heaven, in the sky and on the mountains, the Lord Narayana abides supporting all this.
What need to say more? This world of moving and unmoving, from Brahma down to a blade of grass, all has Narayana as its self.
I see nothing here higher than Narayana, O brahmins; by him all this, seen and unseen, moving and unmoving, is pervaded.
The waters are Vishnu's abode, and he is the lord of the waters; therefore one should always remember Narayana, remover of sin, in the waters.
Especially at the time of bathing, standing pure in the water, one should remember Narayana, meditate on him and place the mantra on the hands and body.
One should place Om and Na on the thumbs of both hands, and the rest on the forefingers and others up to the palm.
One should place Om on the left foot and Na on the right; Mo on the left hip and Na on the right;
Ra on the navel, Ya on the left arm, Na on the right, and Ya on the head.
Below, above, in the heart, at the sides, behind and in front, having meditated on Narayana, the wise one should then begin the armour:
I am the god Narayana, bearing conch, discus and mace. Having meditated thus on oneself, one should utter this mantra:

You are fire, lord of the two-footed, bearer of seed, kindler of desire, chief of all beings, imperishable lord of living creatures.
brahmapuran:60:45	You are the churning-source of nectar, source of the gods, lord of waters; take away all my sin, O king of holy places; salutation to you.
Having uttered this duly, one should then bathe; otherwise, O best of brahmins, bathing there is not commended.
Having performed the sprinkling and cleansing with Vedic mantras, one should then recite the Aghamarshana three times under the water.
As the horse sacrifice, O brahmins, is the rite that removes all sins, so the Aghamarshana hymn here destroys all sins.
Coming out and putting on two clean washed garments, restraining the breath, sipping water and performing the twilight worship of the sun,
one should then stand, casting upward a handful of flowers and water, and worship the sun with raised arms, with the verses marked by him.
One should recite the purifying goddess Gayatri a hundred and eight times, and other solar mantras, standing composed.
Having circumambulated the sun, bowed and sat down facing east, having done one's Vedic study, one should offer libations to the deities and sages,
to men, the ancestors and others, with their names and lineages, knowing the mantras, with water mixed with sesame, duly and with composure.
Having first performed the libations to the deities with composure, the twice-born then becomes qualified for the libations to the ancestors.
At a shraddha and at the time of fire offering one should offer with one hand; at libations one should use both — this is always the rule.
With the right hand supported by the left, one should pour, saying "May he be satisfied," with name and lineage, keeping silence.
One who out of delusion offers libations to the ancestors with sesame taken from his body satisfies the ancestors with skin, flesh, blood and bones.
One should not offer libations to the gods and ancestors with sesame from the limbs; that water becomes blood and the giver becomes sinful.
Water given onto the ground while the giver stands in the water is in vain, O tigers among sages; it reaches no one.
The man who stands on land and gives water into the water — that water does not reach the ancestors and is useless.
One should never offer water to the ancestors into water; coming out, one should perform the water libation on a clean spot.
Not into water, not into vessels, not in anger, not with one hand; water not given onto the ground does not reach them.
The earth has been given by me as the imperishable place of the ancestors, O brahmins; therefore it should be given there by one who desires the ancestors' pleasure.
They were born on the surface of the earth, they rest on the earth, and they dissolve into the earth; therefore one should give water on the earth.
Spreading kusha grass with its tips intact and invoking them with their own mantras — the gods on eastward-pointing tips and the ancestors on southward-pointing ones —
Having drawn the mandala thus, O brahmins, one should worship there the unborn, all-pervading Narayana by the rite of the eight syllables.
Next I shall tell the excellent purification of the body. Meditating on the syllable A in the heart, joined with the lines of a discus,
blazing with three flames, burning, destroying sin; one should contemplate the syllable Ra on the head, in the middle of the orb of the moon,
white in colour, raining nectar and flooding the earth; thus, with sins shaken off, one then becomes of divine body.
The wise one should then place the eight-syllable mantra on himself, beginning with the left foot and placing in order.
The practitioner should perform the fivefold limb-placement of Vishnu and the fourfold manifestation, and purify the hands with the root mantra,
placing each letter separately on the fingers. One should place Om, the white earth, on the left foot;
Na, belonging to Shambhu, dark, is placed on the right; Mo they call time — one should place it on the left hip;
Na, the seed of all, is placed on the right; Ra they call fire — it is placed at the navel;
this Ya, belonging to the wind, rests on the left shoulder; Na should be known as all-pervading, placed on the right shoulder; and this Ya is on the head, where the worlds are established.

Om, salutation to Vishnu — the head; "Om, salutation to the blazing one" — the crest; "Om, salutation to Vishnu" — the armour; "Om, salutation to Vishnu" — the flashing, for binding the directions; "Om hum phat" — the weapon; "Om, on the head, the white Vasudeva"; "Om Am, on the forehead, the red Sankarshana, Garuda, fire, splendour, the sun"; "Om Am, on the neck, the yellow Pradyumna, wind and cloud"; "Om Am, on the heart, the dark Aniruddha, endowed with all powers." Having thus made oneself the fourfold manifestation, one should then perform the rite.

Vishnu stands before me, Keshava behind, Govinda on the right side and Madhusudana on the left,
brahmapuran:61:15	Vaikuntha above, Varaha on the surface of the earth, and in all the intermediate directions Madhava.
brahmapuran:61:16	Whether going or standing, waking or sleeping, my protection is made by Narasimha; I am made of Vasudeva.
Having thus become made of Vishnu, one should then begin the rite; as in the body, so in the deity one should place all the principles.
Then one should perform the sprinkling with the pranava, ending with "phat," declared to remove all obstacles and auspicious.
There one should contemplate the orbs of the sun, moon and fire, and in the middle of the lotus place Vishnu, of wind and of space.
Then contemplating in the heart the syllable Om whose form is light, seated on the pericarp, the eternal form of light,
one should place the eight-syllable mantra in order; worship with it, separately and together, is remembered as supreme.
One should worship the eternal god with the twelve-syllable mantra; then, having fixed him in the heart, one should place him outside on the pericarp,
contemplating the four-armed, mighty one, radiant as a crore of suns, the great yogin, the eternal form of light; then, contemplating in the mind, one should invoke him with the mantra in order.
The invocation mantra: "Fish in form, Boar, Man-Lion and Dwarf — may the boon-giving god Narayana come before me. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation."
The installation mantra: "Here on the pericarp, on this fine seat, is a seat made of lotus; for the good of all beings, stay, O Madhusudana. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation."
The offering mantra: "Om, salutation to the lord of the lords of the three worlds, the god of gods, Hrishikesha, Vishnu. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation."
The foot-water mantra: "Om, O god, eternal Padmanabha, Vishnu, lotus-eyed Madhusudana, accept this water for the feet. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation."
The madhuparka mantra: "O great god, the madhuparka prepared for you by Brahma and the others, offered by me with devotion — accept it, O Purushottama. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation."
The pure white water of the Mandakini, removing all sins — accept this water for sipping, offered by me with devotion. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation.
You are water and earth, you are light and wind; O lord of the world, merely as a gesture I bathe you with water. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation.
O you endowed with the divine principle, joined with the colour of sacrifice, these two garments of golden radiance are yours, O Keshava. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation.
I do not know your body or your movements, O Keshava; accept the perfume offered by me and let it be applied. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation.
I offer you a sacred thread, threefold by the one born of the lotus through the mantras of Rig, Yajus and Saman, joined with the knot of Savitri. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation.
O you endowed with divine jewels, radiant as fire and sun, may your limbs shine with ornaments, O Madhava. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation.

One should worship with "Om namah" for each syllable, or with the whole root mantra. "This incense, the divine essence of trees, rich in fragrance and sweet-smelling, offered to you by me with devotion — accept it. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation."
Light equal to the sun and moon, and to lightning and fire — you alone are the god of lights; accept this lamp. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation.
Food of four kinds joined with the six tastes, offered by me with devotion, is your food offering, O Keshava. Om, salutation to Narayana, salutation.
One should place Vasudeva on the eastern petal, Sankarshana on the southern, Pradyumna on the western and Aniruddha on the northern;
Varaha in the south-east, Narasimha in the south-west, Madhava in the north-west and Trivikrama in the north-east.
Likewise one should place Garuda before the god of the eight syllables, the discus on his left side and the conch on the right;
and the great mace on the god's right; then the wise one should place the Sharnga bow on the god's left,
the two divine quivers on the right and the sword on the left; placing Shri on the right, one should place Pushti on the north,
and the forest garland in front, then the Shrivatsa and Kaustubha; one should place the heart and the other limbs in the four directions beginning with the east,
then the weapon of the god of gods in the corner. Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirriti, Varuna,
Vayu, the lord of wealth, Ishana and Ananta with Brahma one should worship with Tantric mantras, below and above likewise.
Having thus worshipped the lord of gods Janardana in the mandala, a man obtains the desires he wishes; there is no doubt.
Whoever sees Janardana in the mandala worshipped by this very rite enters the imperishable Vishnu.
One by whom Keshava has been worshipped even once by this rite crosses birth, death and old age and attains the state of Vishnu.
For one who tirelessly remembers Narayana with devotion constantly, day after day, Shvetadvipa is prepared as his dwelling.
Joined with Om at the beginning and brightened by "namah" at the end, that name of all the principles is called a mantra.
By this same method one should offer perfume and flowers, performing it for each one in order as prescribed.
Then one should form the mudras as prompted in the prescribed order, and the knower of mantras should perform recitation with the root mantra —
twenty-eight, or eight, or a hundred and eight times, and for desired ends as prescribed, according to one's ability, with composure.
Lotus, conch, Shrivatsa, mace, Garuda, discus, sword and Sharnga — eight mudras are declared.
Go, go to the supreme abode, O ancient Purushottama, where the gods beginning with Brahma find the supreme state.
Those who do not know the worship of Hari with the mantras as told should always worship Achyuta there with the root mantra.
They obtain a thousandfold the fruit of other holy places, those who offer rice-balls to the ancestors there according to rule;
their ancestors obtain imperishable satisfaction. Thus I have properly told the fruit of bathing in the ocean,
and the fruit of giving, O brahmins, and of offering rice-balls — it gives the fruits of dharma, wealth and liberation, and brings long life, fame and glory,
yields enjoyment and liberation to men, is blessed, destroys bad dreams, removes all sins, is holy and grants the fruit of every desire.
This Purana should not be told to an atheist, O best of brahmins. The holy places roar each with its own greatness
only until the greatness of the king of holy places is described, O brahmins. Pushkara and the other holy places give their own fruit,
but the king of holy places gives the fruit of all holy places. Whatever holy places, rivers and lakes there are on earth
enter the ocean; therefore it has attained pre-eminence. The ocean, lord of rivers, is the king of all holy places;
therefore it is superior to all holy places and grants every desire. As darkness perishes when the sun has risen, O brahmins,
so by bathing in the king of holy places sin is destroyed. There has not been and will not be a holy place equal to the king of holy places,
where the Lord Narayana has his abode. Who can tell the virtues of the king of holy places, O brahmins,
where there are ninety-nine crores of holy places? Therefore whatever is done there — bathing, giving, fire offering, recitation, worship of the gods — becomes imperishable, O brahmins.
Having uttered this duly, bathed, satisfied the gods, sages, ancestors and others with sesame water, sipped water and kept silence,
having offered rice-balls to the ancestors and worshipped Purushottama, a man obtains fully the fruit of ten horse sacrifices.
Raising seven generations below and seven above, like a god, he goes to Vishnu's world in a celestial car that moves at will.
Having enjoyed pleasant enjoyments there as long as the moon, sun and stars endure, falling from there and coming here, he surely obtains liberation.
Having thus performed the Panchatirtha and fasted on the eleventh, whoever sees Purushottama on the fifteenth of the bright fortnight of Jyeshtha,
obtaining the fruit described before and sporting in Achyuta's abode, goes to the supreme place from which there is no return.
Leaving aside other months beginning with Magha, O great grandsire, why do you praise Jyeshtha? Tell us the reason, O Lord.

Listen, O tigers among sages; I shall tell briefly why I praise the month of Jyeshtha again and again above them.
brahmapuran:63:12	The holy places on earth, the rivers and lakes, lotus pools, tanks, step-wells, wells and pools,
brahmapuran:63:13	the various rivers and the oceans always come in person to Purushottama for seven days beginning from the bright tenth of Jyeshtha.
brahmapuran:63:14	Therefore whatever bathing, giving and seeing of the deity is done there at that time becomes imperishable, O brahmins.
brahmapuran:63:15	The tenth of the bright fortnight in the month of Jyeshtha, O best of brahmins, takes away ten sins; therefore it is remembered as Dashahara.
brahmapuran:63:16	The man who, well controlled, sees the plough-bearer, Krishna and Bhadra on that day is freed from all sins and goes to Vishnu's world.
brahmapuran:63:17	At the northern and southern solstices, O brahmins, having seen Purushottama, Rama and Subhadra, a man goes to Vishnu's world.
brahmapuran:63:18	The man who, being devout, sees Govinda Purushottama on the swing on the Phalguni full moon goes to Govinda's city.
brahmapuran:63:19	When the equinox arrives, having performed the Panchatirtha according to rule and seen Sankarshana, Krishna and Bhadra, O brahmins,
brahmapuran:63:20	a man obtains the rare fruit of all sacrifices; freed from all sins, he goes to Vishnu's world.
brahmapuran:63:21	Whoever sees Krishna anointed with sandal on the third of the dark fortnight of Vaishakha goes to Achyuta's temple.
brahmapuran:63:22	Whoever sees Purushottama on the full moon of Jyeshtha joined with the Jyeshtha asterism raises twenty-one generations and goes to Vishnu's world.
Householders, graduates, ascetics and celibate students then bathe Krishna, seated on the platform with the plough-armed one.
Likewise all the holy places mentioned before, O best of brahmins, bathe them separately with their own waters mixed with flowers.
Then with kettledrums, conches and the like, with the sounds of drums and tabors, with horns, cymbals, mridangas and jharjharas,
and other various instruments adorned with the sound of bells, with women's auspicious cries and charming sounds of praise,
with cries of victory, hymns and the sounds of lute and flute, a very great sound is heard, like the roaring ocean.
With the Vedic recitation of the sages and other sounds of mantras, with the holy sounds of various hymns enriched by the sound of the Saman,
ascetics, graduates, householders and celibate students praise him with supreme joy at the time of bathing, O best of gods.
By youthful courtesans bent with the weight of their breasts, in yellow and red garments, bent with garlands,
with divine jewelled earrings and golden clusters, Rama and Keshava are fanned with chowries with jewelled handles.
Surrounded by Yakshas, Vidyadharas, Siddhas, Kinnaras and hosts of Apsarases, and by gods, Gandharvas and Charanas in the sky,
the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, hosts of Maruts, guardians of the worlds and others praise Purushottama:

Salutation to you, lord of the god of gods, ancient Purushottama, god who makes creation, sustenance and end, lord of the worlds, master of the universe.
brahmapuran:65:22	We bow with devotion to the god who upholds the three worlds, friendly to brahmins, the cause of liberation, granting the fruit of every desire.
Having thus praised Krishna, the mighty Rama and Subhadra, the gods, O best of sages, stood in the sky.
The divine Gandharvas sing, the Apsarases dance, the instruments of the gods are played, and very cool winds blow.
Then the clouds moving in the sky rain flowers mixed with water, and sages, Siddhas and Charanas raise cries of victory,
all the gods led by Shakra, the sages and ancestors, the lords of creatures, the Nagas and other heaven-dwellers.
Then with auspicious provisions, led by rites and mantras, the hosts of gods, taking the materials for consecration —
Indra, the mighty Vishnu, the sun and moon, Dhatri and Vidhatri, wind and fire,
Pushan, Bhaga, Aryaman, Tvashtri, Amshu with Vivasvan, the wise one with his two wives, with Mitra and Varuna,
the Lord surrounded by Rudras, Vasus, Adityas and the Ashvins, with the Vishvedevas, Maruts, Sadhyas and ancestors,
with Gandharvas and Apsarases, Yakshas, Rakshasas and serpents, with countless divine sages and excellent brahmin sages,
with Vaikhanasas, Valakhilyas, air-eaters and ray-drinkers, with Bhrigus and Angirases well established in all knowledge,
surrounded by all holy Vidyadharas and those perfected in yoga; the Grandsire, Pulastya, Pulaha of great austerity,
Angiras, Kashyapa, Atri, Marichi and Bhrigu, Kratu, Hara, Prachetas, Manu and Daksha,
the seasons, planets and luminaries, O best of brahmins, the embodied rivers and the eternal gods,
oceans, pools and various holy places, earth, heaven, the directions and the trees, O best of brahmins,
Aditi mother of the gods, Hri, Shri, Svaha, Sarasvati, Uma, Shachi, Sinivali, Anumati and Kuhu,
Raka and Dhishana and other wives of the heaven-dwellers, Himavan, Vindhya and many-peaked Meru,
Airavata with his followers, kalas and kashthas, half-months, months and seasons, nights, days and years,
Uchchaihshravas the best of horses, the king of Nagas and Vamana, Aruna and Garuda, trees with herbs,
and the Lord Dharma came together; Time, Yama, Death and Yama's followers,
and the various hosts of gods not named because of their multitude — they come from here and there for the god's consecration.
Then, O brahmins, all the gods, dwellers of heaven, taking the materials of consecration and all auspicious things,
with golden pitchers joined with divine provisions, with holy waters of the Sarasvati and divine waters,
with water of the heavenly Ganga, standing on the earth, they bathe Krishna together with Rama with golden pots containing flowers.
The celestial cars of the gods move in the sky, high and low, divine, moving at will and steady,
variegated with divine jewels, attended by hosts of Apsarases, adorned all around with songs, music and banners.
Thus, O best of sages, having bathed Krishna together with Rama and Subhadra, they joyfully praise them:
Having praised thus, the gods led by Shakra, glad at heart, the hosts of Siddhas and Charanas and other heaven-dwellers,
the sages and Valakhilyas, bowed to Krishna together with Rama and to Subhadra, O best of sages, and stood in the sky.
Having seen, praised and bowed to Krishna, Rama and Subhadra, those dwellers of heaven go each to their own abode.
Then the celestial cars of the gods move in the sky, high and low, divine, moving at will and steady,
variegated with divine jewels, attended by hosts of Apsarases, adorned all around with songs, music and banners.
Mortals who see Purushottama, Balabhadra and Subhadra at that time go to the imperishable state.
Having seen Purushottama on the platform with Subhadra and Rama, they go to the faultless abode; there is no doubt.
